mainTopic: How strong is the bond (זיקה) between a יבמה and the יבם? The גמרא proves that the זיקה gives her only a 'doubtful' (ספק) status, like a ספק ארוסה or ספק נשואה, and uses this to explain the property rulings in our משנה.
overview: The גמרא explains the משנה about a שומרת יבם (a widow waiting for יבום) who receives property. It proves that the זיקה gives her only a doubtful status: זיקת ארוסה עושה ספק ארוסה, shown from בית הלל letting her sell, and זיקת נשואה עושה ספק נשואה, shown from בית שמאי splitting her property after death. רבה challenges this reading, because the dispute should then have appeared over the produce while she is alive. He offers his own explanation instead. While she lives, her claim is certain and the יבם's claim is only doubtful, and a ספק cannot take from a ודאי. After she dies, both sets of heirs come to inherit, so they split. אביי objects with the collapsed-house משנה, where בית שמאי let a doubtful creditor share with the certain heirs. רבה answers that בית שמאי hold שטר העומד לגבות כגבוי דמי, and he proves it from the סוטה משנה. The גמרא then explains why אביי did not challenge from the סוטה case or from the כתובה in our משנה, with רב אשי supporting the answer from the משנה's wording. Finally אביי gives his own answer: the two parts of the משנה deal with property that came to her at different times.

steps.title: The second half of the principle: a married woman's bond creates a doubtful marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes stating its principle: the זיקה of a woman who was fully married gives her the status of a ספק נשואה toward the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The levirate bond of a married woman makes her like a woman who is doubtfully married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a two-part rule it has been stating. If the widow was fully married to her late husband, her connection to the יבם is like a doubtful marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זיקה copies the same level of relationship the woman had with her first husband, but in a weaker form. A full marriage becomes a 'maybe-marriage' (ספק נשואה) with the יבם. This weaker status is what explains the property rules in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The levirate bond that links a widow to her late husband's brother (the יבם)
A fully married woman (after נישואין, not just engaged)
Doubt, a status we are not sure about
Makes, creates

phrases.english: The bond of a married woman makes her a doubtfully married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part principle whose first half (about an ארוסה) was stated just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זיקה with a woman who was נשואה gives her only ספק נשואה status toward the יבם.

steps.title: Why the engaged woman's bond must be only a doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts proving the first half: if the זיקה made her a definite ארוסה, בית הלל would not allow her to sell property, yet in our משנה they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bond of an engaged woman makes her a doubtfully engaged woman. For if you thought she was definitely engaged, would בית הלל agree that she may sell and give away the property, and that it is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a proof by asking a pointed question. If she were definitely engaged, would בית הלל really let her sell? The source showing they would not comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that a שומרת יבם may sell and give away property she received. The גמרא hints that this cannot fit with a definite engagement. It will soon show that בית הלל forbid a definite ארוסה from selling לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed (engaged) woman, after קידושין but before נישואין
For if it would enter your mind, if you were to think
Definitely, certainly
They agree
And it is valid, it stands

phrases.english: The bond of an engaged woman makes her a doubtfully engaged woman —
for if you were to think she is a definitely engaged woman,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדִים בֵּית הִלֵּל שֶׁמּוֹכֶרֶת וְנוֹתֶנֶת וְקַיָּים?
phrases.english: would בית הלל agree that she may sell and give, and it is valid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the first half of the principle (about an ארוסה) and begins proving it.
steps.raayaObject: That the זיקה of an ארוסה gives only ספק ארוסה status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, where בית הלל agree the שומרת יבם may sell and give away property.

steps.title: The משנה in כתובות: בית הלל forbid an engaged woman to sell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that בית הלל say a definitely engaged woman may not sell property she received after engagement, though a sale done anyway is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: If property came to her after she became engaged, בית שמאי say she may sell it, and בית הלל say she may not sell it. Both agree that if she did sell or give it away, the sale is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that backs up its question. בית הלל hold that a definite ארוסה may not sell such property לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here: לכתחילה (may she sell from the start?) and בדיעבד (if she already sold, does it stand?). For a definite ארוסה, בית הלל say no לכתחילה, but the sale stands בדיעבד. Our משנה lets the שומרת יבם sell even לכתחילה, so her status must be weaker than a definite ארוסה.

keyTerms.meaning: Property came to her, usually by inheritance
She may sell
These and those, meaning both sides

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two levels. 'מכרה ונתנה קיים' means that after the fact the sale stands. It does NOT mean בית הלל let her sell from the start. That difference is the whole proof.

phrases.english: But we learned: If property came to her after she became engaged,
phrases.notes: כתובות 78a

phrases.english: בית שמאי say: She may sell,
and בית הלל say: She may not sell.
Both of them agree
that if she sold or gave it away, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the pointed question in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That according to בית הלל a definite ארוסה may not sell לכתחילה.

steps.title: Conclusion: the engaged woman's bond is only a doubtful engagement
steps.stepSummary: Since בית הלל let the שומרת יבם sell from the start, the זיקה must make her only a ספק ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the bond of an engaged woman makes her a doubtfully engaged woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the first proof. The bond of an engaged widow is only a 'maybe-engagement'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A definite ארוסה may not sell לכתחילה according to בית הלל. Yet בית הלל let the שומרת יבם sell. So her bond to the יבם must be weaker, only a doubt, and that is why she keeps full power to sell.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, so it must be
Learn from this, conclude from it
A woman whose engagement is in doubt

steps.whatToRemember: זיקת ארוסה עושה ספק ארוסה: the bond with an engaged widow is only a doubtful engagement. That is why even בית הלל let her sell property לכתחילה.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
the bond of an engaged woman makes her a doubtfully engaged woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from comparing our משנה with the משנה in כתובות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The זיקה of an ארוסה creates only a ספק ארוסה status.

steps.title: Starting the proof for the married woman's bond
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins proving the second half: if the זיקה made her a definite נשואה, why would בית שמאי say the inheritance is split between the husband's heirs and the father's heirs?
steps.simpleTranslation: The bond of a married woman makes her a doubtfully married woman. For if you thought she was definitely married, would בית שמאי say that the husband's heirs split with the father's heirs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the second half of the rule and sets up a proof for it. It uses the same kind of pointed question, now aimed at בית שמאי's ruling in our משנה; the explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says that if the שומרת יבם dies, בית שמאי rule that her husband's heirs and her father's heirs divide the property. Splitting is the kind of ruling used when there is a doubt. The גמרא hints that this would not fit if she were definitely married, which supports calling her a ספק נשואה.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide, they split it
The husband's heirs
The father's heirs (her own family's heirs)

phrases.english: The bond of a married woman makes her a doubtfully married woman.
For if you were to think she is a definitely married woman,
would בית שמאי say

phrases.aramaic: יַחְלוֹקוּ יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב?
phrases.english: that the husband's heirs divide it with the father's heirs?
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה's ruling for when the waiting widow dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the proof for the ארוסה half, the גמרא turns to prove the נשואה half, using the same 'if you were to think' structure.
steps.raayaObject: That the זיקה of a נשואה gives only ספק נשואה status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית שמאי's ruling in our משנה that the husband's heirs and the father's heirs divide the property.

steps.title: A definite husband takes back property even from buyers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: when property comes to a married woman, everyone agrees her husband can take it back even from people who bought it from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: if property came to her after she was married, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that if she sold it or gave it away, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the question from step 5 with a משנה. A real husband has strong rights, strong enough to take property back from buyers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the זיקה made her a definite נשואה, the יבם would have the full rights of a real husband. A real husband's heirs would get everything, and nobody would split it. So the split בית שמאי rule in our משנה does not fit with a definite marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: She was fully married (after the wedding, not just engaged)
Both sides (בית שמאי and בית הלל) agree
Buyers
Takes away from the hands of

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כתובות 78a.

phrases.english: If property came to her after she was married,
both these and those agree
that if she sold it or gave it away,
the husband takes it out of the hands of the buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that sharpens step 5's question: a definite husband has full rights, so splitting the property makes no sense.
steps.raayaObject: That the זיקה does not make her a definite נשואה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כתובות: the husband takes back property even from buyers

steps.title: So the bond makes her only a doubtful married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the זיקה of a married woman gives her the status of a ספק נשואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the bond of a married woman makes her a doubtful married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the second proof. Because the property is split, she must be only a doubtful married woman toward the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A split fits a doubt: the יבם's side might be a husband or might not be. This completes the support for both halves of the principle from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; conclude from here
A woman about whom it is doubtful whether she is married

steps.whatToRemember: The first explanation reads בית הלל's sale rule as showing ספק ארוסה, and בית שמאי's split as showing ספק נשואה.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
the bond of a married woman makes her a doubtful married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in steps 5-6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The זיקה of a fully married woman makes her only a ספק נשואה toward the יבם.

steps.title: Why not argue about the produce while she is alive?
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges the explanation: if this were the point, the משנה should have shown the argument in a simpler case, about the produce while she is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Instead of arguing about the property itself after her death, let them argue about the produce while she is alive!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the explanation just given, which was עולא's. He says the way the משנה is built does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the later case is about a woman who was doubtfully married, the dispute should already show up while she is alive. The question would be who eats the produce, since a husband gets the produce of his wife's property. The fact that the משנה only discusses after-death ownership suggests the explanation is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of arguing about
The property itself (its ownership)
Produce or income from the property

phrases.english: רבה said to him:
Instead of arguing about the property itself, after her death,
phrases.notes: "Itself" means the actual ownership of the property, as opposed to its produce.

phrases.english: let them argue about while she is alive, and about the produce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the משנה that the conclusion in step 7 was built on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of the משנה's later clause as showing ספק נשואה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she is doubtfully married, the dispute would already exist during her life over the produce, so the משנה should have taught that simpler, earlier case.

steps.title: רבה: while she is alive, a doubt cannot take from her
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that both parts of the משנה deal with a fully married woman who is a ספק נשואה. While she is alive she holds the property, and a doubtful claim cannot take it from a certain one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: Both parts deal with a woman who fell to the יבם when she was fully married, and the bond of a married woman makes her a doubtful married woman. In the first part, where she is alive, she is the certain one and they are the doubtful ones, and a doubt cannot take away from a certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his own explanation of the משנה. He keeps the idea of ספק נשואה but explains the two parts differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no argument about the produce during her life, because she has a certain claim to her own property. The יבם is only maybe a husband, and a doubtful claim never takes away from a certain claim. That is why she may sell, and why the משנה does not show any dispute while she is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one (both parts)
The first part of the משנה
Certain, definite
A doubtful claim cannot take away from a certain one

steps.confusionAlert: רבה agrees that the זיקה makes her a ספק נשואה. He only changes how the two parts of the משנה are explained.

phrases.english: Rather, רבה said:
Both this and that are where she fell to the יבם when she was married,
and the bond of a married woman makes her a doubtful married woman.
In the first part, where she is alive,

phrases.aramaic: הָוְיָא לַהּ אִיהִי וַדַּאי וְאִינְהוּ סָפֵק,
phrases.english: she is the certain one and they are the doubtful ones,
phrases.notes: "They" means the יבם's side, who is only maybe a husband.

phrases.english: and a doubt cannot take away from a certainty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's own challenge by offering a new reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: both clauses are about a fully married woman, and they differ in whether she is alive or dead.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two parts of the משנה deal with different kinds of women, so the dispute should appear during her life too.
steps.terutzMaskana: While she lives, her certain ownership beats the יבם's doubtful claim, so there is nothing to argue about.

steps.title: After her death, both sides split
steps.stepSummary: In the later part, after she died, no one has a certain claim. The father's heirs and the husband's heirs both come to inherit, so they divide the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the later part, where she died, these come to inherit and those come to inherit, so they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his explanation by explaining the later part of the משנה, the case after her death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she dies, her certain claim is gone. Both sides are now heirs with doubtful, equal claims: her father's heirs and the husband's heirs. Since neither is certain, the property is split, and this is why בית שמאי's split appears only after death.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
To inherit
They divide

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, while she is alive, her certain claim beats the יבם's doubt. After she dies, two equal doubtful claims means the property is divided.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key monetary rule: a doubt cannot take from someone who has a certain claim, but when both sides are equally doubtful, they split.

phrases.english: In the later part, where she died,
these come to inherit,
phrases.notes: "These" are the father's heirs and "those" are the husband's heirs.

phrases.english: and those come to inherit,
so they divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's answer by explaining the after-death clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: alive (certain against doubt) versus dead (doubt against doubt).
steps.terutzMaskana: After death, both sides of heirs have equal doubtful claims, so they split the property.

steps.title: אביי questions רבה's rule and starts quoting a משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether בית שמאי really hold that a doubtful claim cannot take from a certain one. He begins quoting a משנה about a house that collapsed on a man and his father, where the man owed money to his wife and to a creditor.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Is it true that according to בית שמאי a doubtful claim cannot take property from a certain claim? But we learned in a משנה: A house fell on a man and his father, or on him and the people he would inherit from. He owed money for his wife's כתובה and to a creditor.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's explanation and starts setting up a case from another משנה. This line lays out the facts that the next steps build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said that for בית שמאי a ספק cannot take from a ודאי. אביי wants to show a case where בית שמאי do let a ספק take. First he gives the facts: father and son died together, and the son had debts.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubtful claim cannot take property away from a certain claim
The people he would inherit from
The money a husband owes his wife under her marriage contract
A creditor, someone he owes money to

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection against him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, who just gave the explanation in the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבֵית שַׁמַּאי אֵין סָפֵק מוֹצִיא מִידֵי וַדַּאי?
phrases.english: And according to Beit Shammai, can a doubtful claim not take from a certain claim?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל אָבִיו,
phrases.english: But we learned: A house fell on him and on his father,
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא בתרא 157a.

phrases.english: on him and on those he inherits from,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ עָלָיו כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה וּבַעַל חוֹב.
phrases.english: and he owed a wife's marriage contract and a creditor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule רבה used in step 9 to explain the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that for בית שמאי a ספק cannot take from a ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows בית שמאי dividing property even though one side is ודאי and the other is ספק.

steps.title: The two sides argue over who died first
steps.stepSummary: The father's heirs say the son died first, so the son never inherited and the creditor gets nothing. The creditor says the father died first, so the son inherited and the creditor can collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father's heirs say: The son died first, and then the father died. The creditor says: The father died first, and then the son died.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out each side's claim. Everything depends on who died first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son died first, he never owned his father's property, so his creditor cannot collect from it. If the father died first, the son inherited it for a moment, and then the creditor can collect from it. Nobody knows which is true.

keyTerms.meaning: The father's heirs
Died first

steps.confusionAlert: The creditor here is the son's creditor, not the father's. He can only collect from the father's property if the son lived long enough to inherit it.

phrases.english: The father's heirs say:
The son died first,
and afterward the father died,
and the creditor says:
The father died first,
and afterward the son died —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה that אביי began in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: Shows that the creditor's claim is only doubtful
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that for בית שמאי a ספק cannot take from a ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The creditor's claim depends on an unknowable order of death, so it is only a ספק against the father's heirs, who inherit no matter what.

steps.title: בית שמאי say divide; בית הלל say the property stays where it was
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי rule that the father's heirs and the creditor split the property. בית הלל rule that the property stays with its last known owner, the father's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: They should divide it. בית הלל say: The property stays in its previous status.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ruling of each side. This ruling is the part אביי will use against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל leave the property with the father's heirs, since it was last known to belong to the father. בית שמאי give the creditor half, even though his claim is only a maybe.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide the property
The property stays with its last known owner

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: They divide,
and Beit Hillel say: The property stays in its prior status.
phrases.notes: Here that means the property stays with the father's heirs, because it was last known to be the father's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted משנה with the ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that for בית שמאי a ספק cannot take from a ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי rule יחלוקו, giving the doubtful creditor half the property held by the certain heirs.

steps.title: אביי's point: here a doubtful claim takes from a certain claim
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the father's heirs have a certain claim and the creditor only a doubtful one. Since בית שמאי still divide, a ספק does take from a ודאי, which goes against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, the father's heirs are certain and the creditor is doubtful, and yet the doubtful claim comes and takes from the certain one!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי spells out why the משנה is a problem for רבה. This is the punchline of his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's heirs inherit no matter what, so their claim is certain. The creditor collects only if the father died first, so his claim is a maybe. בית שמאי still give him half, which contradicts רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But here, in this case
And yet it comes

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's challenge: in the house-collapse משנה, בית שמאי let a doubtful creditor take half from heirs whose claim is certain. So רבה cannot say that for בית שמאי a ספק never takes from a ודאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבה's whole explanation of the ספק נשואה case rested on this rule. If the rule fails for בית שמאי, his explanation is in danger.

phrases.english: But here, the father's heirs are certain,
and the creditor is doubtful,
and the doubtful one comes and takes from the certain one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the quoted משנה to finish אביי's objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule from step 9 that a ספק cannot take from a ודאי, as applied to בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heirs' claim is certain and the creditor's is doubtful, yet בית שמאי divide. So for בית שמאי a ספק can take from a ודאי.

steps.title: בית שמאי treat a debt document as already collected
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי: בית שמאי hold that a debt in a שטר waiting to be collected counts as already collected, so the creditor is not a mere ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that a document that is waiting to be collected is treated as if it were already collected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's challenge. He explains that the creditor in the collapsed-house case is treated as if he already holds his money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that the creditor had only a doubtful claim against the heirs' certain claim. רבה says that for בית שמאי, a written debt counts as already in the creditor's hands. So both sides are equally 'holding' the property, and splitting it does not mean a ספק took from a ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold / they are of the opinion
A written legal document, here a document of debt
That is waiting to be collected
It is considered as if already collected

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle saves רבה's rule. The split in the collapsed-house case is explained by the שטר, not by a ספק overpowering a ודאי.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
a document that is waiting to be collected
phrases.notes: He means the creditor's debt document from the collapsed-house case.

phrases.english: is considered as if already collected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from the collapsed-house משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the creditor's status so the case no longer counts as a ספק against a ודאי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The creditor has only a doubtful claim, so בית שמאי's split shows that a ספק can take from a ודאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: For בית שמאי the creditor is treated as already holding the debt, so he stands equal to the heirs and they split.

steps.title: Source: the suspected wives whose husbands died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that בית שמאי hold this rule and quotes a משנה about סוטות whose husbands died before they drank.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? We learned in a משנה: if the husbands died before the women drank, בית שמאי say the women collect their כתובה and do not drink. בית הלל say either they drink, or they do not collect their כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know בית שמאי hold this rule. It quotes a משנה as the source, and the proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about a wife suspected of being unfaithful who was supposed to drink the bitter waters to clear herself. Her husband died before she drank. בית שמאי let her collect her כתובה, while בית הלל do not let her collect unless she drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asking for a source)
Drank / drink: the bitter waters of a סוטה
Their כתובה: the money promised to a wife in her marriage contract
They take / collect

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה has nothing to do with a collapsed house. The גמרא brings a completely different case to show how בית שמאי think about a שטר.

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?
As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in סוטה 24a.

phrases.english: If their husbands died before they drank —
phrases.notes: These are women suspected of being unfaithful, who were supposed to drink the bitter waters.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
They collect their marriage contract money and do not drink.
And Beit Hillel say:
Either they drink
or they do not collect their marriage contract money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the rule stated in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold a שטר waiting to be collected counts as already collected.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוטה about suspected wives whose husbands died before they drank.

steps.title: How could she drink without her husband?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions בית הלל's words 'either they drink': the פסוק requires the husband to bring her, and he is dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Either they drink'?! The Torah said, 'And the man shall bring his wife,' and here there is no husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the wording of בית הלל. How can they offer her the choice to drink when her husband has died?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the husband brings his wife to drink. Once the husband is dead, the drinking ritual cannot happen at all. So 'either they drink' cannot be a real option.

keyTerms.meaning: And the man shall bring his wife (the פסוק about the סוטה)
The Merciful One: the Torah
And there is none: here, there is no husband

phrases.english: "Either they drink"?!
"And the man shall bring his wife"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:15

phrases.english: the Torah said,
and there is no husband here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of בית הלל in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires the husband to bring his wife, so after his death drinking is impossible and cannot be an option.

steps.title: Since they cannot drink, they cannot collect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads בית הלל as meaning: since the women cannot drink, they do not collect their כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since they do not drink, they do not collect their כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what בית הלל really meant. Drinking is not an option; since she cannot drink, she cannot collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking was her only way to prove she was innocent and earn her כתובה. Since the husband died, that way is closed, so בית הלל rule she gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because

phrases.english: Rather:
since they do not drink
they do not collect their marriage contract money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question about בית הלל's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל give the women a real choice to drink.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל mean that since drinking is impossible, the women cannot collect.

steps.title: Her claim is only a doubt, yet she collects
steps.stepSummary: רבה points out that the wife's claim is a ספק, since maybe she was unfaithful, yet בית שמאי let her collect from the heirs, who hold the property for certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is a doubt: maybe she was unfaithful, maybe she was not. And yet the doubt comes and takes out of the hands of the certain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to בית שמאי's side of the משנה. It shows that their ruling cannot be explained just by a ספק taking from a ודאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her right to the כתובה is doubtful, while the husband's heirs hold the property for certain. Even someone who lets a ספק take from a ודאי would only let her split, but בית שמאי give her the whole כתובה. So something else must be giving her strength, and that sets up the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: She was unfaithful
And takes out of the hands of
A certain claim

phrases.english: But here, it is a doubt:
maybe she was unfaithful, maybe she was not,
and the doubtful claim comes
and takes out of the hands of the certain claim!
phrases.notes: The certain side is the husband's heirs, who already hold his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from clarifying בית הלל to drawing the proof from בית שמאי's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי's ruling needs a reason beyond a ספק taking from a ודאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית שמאי's ruling that the wives collect their full כתובה even though their claim is doubtful.

steps.title: Conclusion: a debt document counts as collected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that בית שמאי hold a שטר waiting to be collected counts as already collected. That is why the wife can collect her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: a document waiting to be collected is considered as if already collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the משנה. בית שמאי treat a debt document as already collected, which proves רבה's answer from Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is a document waiting to be collected, so for בית שמאי the wife is treated as if she already holds the money. That explains why she collects even though her claim is doubtful. The same idea explains the creditor in the collapsed-house case, so רבה's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion formula)

steps.whatToRemember: For בית שמאי, a שטר waiting to be collected counts as already collected. So the creditor in the collapsed house and the wife with her כתובה are treated as if they already hold the money. This means בית שמאי never actually let a ספק take from a ודאי, and רבה's rule survives אביי's challenge.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
a document that is waiting to be collected
phrases.notes: Here the document is the wife's marriage contract.

phrases.english: is considered as if already collected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 19 and confirms רבה's answer from Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית שמאי hold that a שטר waiting to be collected counts as already collected. This defends רבה's rule that a ספק cannot take from a ודאי.

steps.title: Why didn't אביי challenge רבה from the סוטה case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי did not use the סוטה משנה to challenge רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי, let him challenge רבה from this משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders why אביי picked a different משנה for his earlier challenge to רבה. The סוטה משנה we just saw seems like a ready-made source he could have used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that a שטר waiting to be collected does NOT count as collected. By that view, the סוטה משנה shows בית שמאי letting a doubtful claim take money from people who own it for certain. That is exactly what אביי wanted to pin on בית שמאי, so why didn't he quote it?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him raise an objection against him (the same root as אֵיתִיבֵיהּ and תְּיוּבְתָּא)
From this source

phrases.english: And Abaye, let him object to him from this!
phrases.notes: "This" means the סוטה משנה from Step 16. "Him" is רבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה used the סוטה משנה for his own view, the גמרא asks why אביי didn't use that same משנה against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's choice of source for his challenge to רבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By אביי's view, the סוטה משנה clearly shows בית שמאי letting a doubtful claim win, so it should have been his obvious source.

steps.title: A woman's כתובה may be special because of חינא
steps.stepSummary: אביי avoided the סוטה case because a כתובה might follow special rules that make a woman attractive for marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a woman's כתובה is different, because of חינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that אביי didn't use the סוטה case because a כתובה is not a regular debt. חכמים may have strengthened it to make women attractive for marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כתובה has extra-strong rules, then בית שמאי letting her collect proves nothing about ordinary debts. So the סוטה case was too weak a source for אביי's general point.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
A woman's marriage contract
Is different
Charm or attractiveness, making her desirable to marry

phrases.english: Perhaps a woman's marriage contract is different,
because of attractiveness.
phrases.notes: Knowing she will collect her כתובה makes a woman more appealing to marry, so חכמים backed it extra strongly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by showing why the סוטה case could not prove a general rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the כתובה has a unique rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוטה משנה is a clear source about debts in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כתובה may have special strength because of חינא, so it cannot prove a rule about ordinary debts.

steps.title: Why not challenge from the כתובה in our own משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי didn't use the כתובה case in our משנה, where בית שמאי say to split.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him challenge רבה from the כתובה in our משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests another source אביי could have used: the end of our own משנה, where a יבמה dies and בית שמאי say to split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה the יבם's side holds the כתובה money for certain, and her father's heirs have only a doubtful claim. If בית שמאי say to split even the כתובה, that would show a doubtful claim taking money from a certain one.

keyTerms.meaning: Of our own משנה
The marriage contract and the money it promises her

phrases.english: So let him object to him from the marriage contract of our mishna!
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה on 38a, where the widow waiting for her יבם dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the סוטה case was set aside, the גמרא offers another source אביי could have used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה seems to show בית שמאי splitting a כתובה between a certain owner and a doubtful claimant, so it should work for אביי.

steps.title: בית שמאי don't argue about the כתובה there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in our משנה, בית שמאי do not actually dispute the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly that our משנה is no source, because בית שמאי don't argue about the כתובה there at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי never said to split the כתובה, our משנה proves nothing about doubtful claims taking money. This short answer is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not disagree

phrases.english: They do not disagree.
phrases.notes: He means that in our משנה, בית שמאי don't argue about the כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by denying that our משנה has a dispute about the כתובה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the premise: there is no dispute about the כתובה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי say to split the כתובה in our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי do not dispute the כתובה in our משנה.

steps.title: But the משנה clearly mentions the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, which seems to put the כתובה inside the dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: They don't disagree?! But the משנה teaches: If she died, what is done with her כתובה and with the property that comes in and goes out with her? בית שמאי say: the husband's heirs split with the father's heirs. בית הלל say: the property stays with whoever holds it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 24 by quoting the משנה word for word. It seems to show that בית שמאי rule on the כתובה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the כתובה and the property together in one question, and then gives one dispute. Read simply, בית שמאי's split applies to both, including the כתובה. That is exactly what Step 24 denied.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught (introduces a quote that contradicts)
Property that comes in and goes out with her: her own property that stays hers
The husband's heirs
The property stays with whoever holds it now

phrases.english: They don't?! But it is taught:
If she died, what should be done with her marriage contract
and with the property that comes in and goes out with her?
phrases.notes: This is property she brought into the marriage. It still belongs to her and leaves with her.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: יַחְלוֹקוּ יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב,
phrases.english: The husband's heirs should divide with the father's heirs,
and Beit Hillel say:
The property stays in its presumed ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 24's claim by quoting the משנה itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית שמאי don't dispute the כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה asks about the כתובה and the property in one question and then gives one dispute, so the split seems to cover the כתובה too.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: the כתובה question is left open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה: the question about the כתובה is raised and left unanswered, and the dispute is only about her property.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: If she died, what is done with her כתובה? It leaves that question. Then: the property that comes in and goes out with her: בית שמאי say the husband's heirs split with the father's heirs, and בית הלל say the property stays with whoever holds it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא splits the משנה into two parts. The כתובה question is asked and dropped, and the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל is only about her property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the dispute is only about her property, בית שמאי's split says nothing about the כתובה. That saves Step 24 and explains why אביי could not use our משנה as his source.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introduces a rereading)
And he left it: the question is dropped without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: אביי could not challenge רבה from the סוטה case, because a כתובה may be special due to חינא. He could not use our משנה either, because there בית שמאי's split covers only her property. The כתובה question is left open.
steps.confusionAlert: The two quotes of the משנה look almost the same. The difference is where the question ends: in the second reading, the כתובה question stops at וְשַׁבְקַהּ, and the dispute begins with a new topic.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
If she died, what should be done with her marriage contract?
And he left it.
phrases.notes: The תנא asks about the כתובה and never answers. Then he moves on to a new case.

phrases.english: Property that comes in and goes out with her:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: יַחְלוֹקוּ יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב,
phrases.english: The husband's heirs should divide with the father's heirs,
and Beit Hillel say:
The property stays in its presumed ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 by rereading the משנה so that the dispute does not include the כתובה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's single dispute covers both the כתובה and the property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתובה question is left open, and the dispute is only about her property, so our משנה cannot serve as אביי's source.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports the new reading
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves from the order of the words in the משנה that בית שמאי's ruling to split is only about her property, not about the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording of our משנה also shows this. It says, 'The husband's heirs split with the father's heirs.' It does not say, 'The father's heirs split with the husband's heirs.' We can learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support from the exact wording of the משנה for the answer in Step 26. That answer said the dispute is only about her property and the כתובה question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever 'splits with' someone is the one coming to take from the side that is already holding the money. The משנה has the husband's heirs coming to split with the father's heirs, so the father's heirs are the ones holding it, and that fits her own property. The כתובה would be held by the husband's heirs, since they are the ones who owe it, so the wording would have been reversed if the כתובה were included.

keyTerms.meaning: is precise; the exact wording shows this
they should divide or split
the husband's heirs
the father's heirs (her family's side)
learn from this; conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: The order of names in 'X splits with Y' tells you who is holding the money: Y holds it and X comes to take a share. This shows that בית שמאי's ruling to split is about her property, not her כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'split with' as completely equal wording that could go either way. The גמרא treats the side named second as the one already holding the money.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא —
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Our Mishnah is also precise this way,
phrases.notes: He means the wording of the משנה backs up the answer the גמרא just gave in Step 26.

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: יַחְלוֹקוּ יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב.
phrases.english: for it teaches: The husband's heirs divide with the father's heirs.
phrases.notes: The husband's heirs are the ones coming to take a share, so the father's heirs must be holding the property.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָתָנֵי: יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל.
phrases.english: And it does not teach: The father's heirs with the husband's heirs.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rereading of the משנה given in Step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that בית שמאי's ruling to split is only about her property and does not cover the כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word order in the משנה: 'the husband's heirs divide with the father's heirs,' and not the other way around.

steps.title: אביי: the two parts of the משנה talk about property received at different times
steps.stepSummary: אביי settles the contradiction in בית שמאי's rulings by saying the first part of the משנה talks about property she got while waiting for the יבם, and the last part talks about property she got while her husband was still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The first part of the משנה is about property that came to her while she was waiting for her יבם. The last part is about property that came to her while she was still married to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer to the original problem: why בית שמאי let her sell in the first part of the משנה but say to split in the last part. He says the two parts describe two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, it looked like בית שמאי ruled two different ways on the same property. אביי says the timing is different in each part. In the first part the property came to her only after her husband died, while she was waiting for the יבם. In the last part it came to her while her husband was still alive. Because the cases are different, the rulings can be different, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: the first part of the משנה
the last part of the משנה
came to her, usually by inheritance
a widow waiting for her יבם to do יבום or חליצה
literally 'under him'; married to him

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's way of solving the problem is to split the case: same woman, but the property reached her at different times, so בית שמאי can rule differently in the two parts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a separate line of answers to the contradiction, so it does not need the rereading of the כתובה wording from Steps 24 to 27.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא דְּנָפְלוּ לָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם,
phrases.english: The first part is where property came to her when she was waiting for her yavam,
phrases.notes: This is the part where בית שמאי say she may sell the property.

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא דְּנָפְלוּ לָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא תַּחְתָּיו דְּבַעַל.
phrases.english: the last part is where it came to her when she was still married to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: רֵישָׁא דְּנָפְלוּ לָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב אשי's line and offers a new, separate answer to the contradiction in בית שמאי's rulings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the first and last parts of the משנה are about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both parts of the משנה are about the same property, so בית שמאי seem to contradict themselves (sell versus split).
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is about property she got while waiting for the יבם, and the last part is about property she got during her marriage, so the different rulings fit together.
